title: Affine chart equivalence carries global sections to triple rings
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] lying over $y\in Y$, and let $\kappa(\bar x)\subset\Omega$ be the separable algebraic closure [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure] of the residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field] in $\Omega$ (with $\kappa(y)\to\Omega$ given by $\bar x$). Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$ be an affine open containing $y$ and $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the prime ideal of $y$, so that $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\kappa(y)$. Let $\mathcal N$ be the category of affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V,\bar v)$ of $\bar x$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods] (a morphism $(V',\bar v')\to(V,\bar v)$ is a $Y$-morphism $V'\to V$ carrying $\bar v'$ to $\bar v$), and let $\mathcal T$ be the category of triples $(B,\mathfrak q,\phi)$ where $A\to B$ is a ring map with $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], $\mathfrak q\subset B$ is a prime lying over $\mathfrak p$, and $\phi:\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\kappa(\bar x)$ is a homomorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebras; a morphism $(B,\mathfrak q,\phi)\to(B',\mathfrak q',\phi')$ is an $A$-algebra map $\beta:B\to B'$ with $\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak q')=\mathfrak q$ and $\phi'\circ\kappa(\beta)=\phi$. Let $\mathcal N_U$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal N$ whose structure map factors through the given open immersion $i:U\to Y$. Assume that every residue embedding $\kappa(v)\to\Omega$ of an object in $\mathcal N_U$ has image in $K=\kappa(\bar x)$. Let $D_U:\mathcal N_U^{op}\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ send $(V,\bar v)$ to $\Gamma(V)$, and let $D_T:\mathcal T\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ be the forgetful ring diagram [def-weil-pbc-etale-residue-triples]. There are an equivalence $E:\mathcal N_U^{op}\simeq\mathcal T$ and a natural ring isomorphism $\delta:D_U\cong E\circ D_T$. For $c=(V,\bar v)$ write $t=E(c)$. For every chart factorization $g:V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, the induced map $A\to\Gamma(V)$ followed by $\delta_c:\Gamma(V)\to B_t$ equals $\alpha_t$. Moreover $\bar v$ followed by $V\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(V)$ is the spectrum map of $B_t\to\kappa(q_t)\to K\to\Omega$ followed by $\operatorname{Spec}(\delta_c)$.
